rationale: This is a direct rediscovery of the published intangible-adjusted book-to-market / R&D-capital value factor (Lev–Sougiannis; Park 2019; Eisfeldt–Kim–Papanikolaou iHML), with no cross-theme content beyond the standard capitalization convention.

The rank-wedge construction is a genuinely different object from either value level and is internally consistent, but it is close to a monotone re-labeling of R&D-stock-to-market (Chan–Lakonishok–Sougiannis), so the test must show it adds beyond that known predictor.

Value-plus-turnover composites are a well-trodden value–quality combination, and dropping COALESCE means TS_SUM(xrd,5) is missing for the large non-R&D-reporting population, so coverage collapses to a selected subsample in a way the reasoning never acknowledges.

This is essentially the reciprocal of the same intangible-adjusted valuation ratio already proposed (hence not an independent signal), and its denominator approaches zero for the many firms with negligible intan and R&D, guaranteeing unstable extreme-decile composition.
The signal is arithmetically E/P plus R&D-to-market, both individually documented predictors, so it is a trivial additive blend of known anomalies rather than a cross-theme interaction.

target_name: Value Tilt Scaled by Intangible Intensity
rationale: The conditional shrinkage is correctly signed and the mechanism (adjustment matters only where intangibles are large) is coherent, but the stated claim of "without shrinking coverage" is false since TS_SUM(xrd,5) without COALESCE restricts the sample to five-year R&D reporters.
